name: Dazz
caption: Billed the Messiah of Metal, a co-founder of Chaos A.D. and of the federation itself, who ran its first weekly show as General Manager and teamed with Violent A one last time on its final broadcast.

tenures.source: The federation's own About page names him a founder in January 2003 and the General Manager of Monday Night Havok; he teams with Violent A against Talent Inc on Ultimate Chaos, 3 April 2007.

Dazz's Motor City contender roleplay (7 September 2009) says he opened the Chaotic Wrestling Federation in January 2003 and came to MCW as General Manager 'mere weeks after the last CWF pay per view'; the staff page of its 2008 site lists a General Manager under his billing; Dazz's Livewire roleplays carry him to the Global title on 21 January 2010.

identity.note: Name collision only: no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's own record ties this character to the same-named records already held at other wings.

Name only: Anarchy Wrestling's Dazz is a newcomer of September 2008 with one opening win and no moniker, hometown or history on record; this Dazz is billed the Messiah of Metal from Toronto, and nothing in either record names the other federation. Revisit if a document ties them.

The same Dazz, billed the Messiah of Metal, of Chaos A.D. and the band Havok Rising: by his own roleplays he opened the predecessor in January 2003, teamed with Violent A on its last broadcast in April 2007, came over when the buyer took on his contract and served MCW as a General Manager.

name: Violent A
caption: A Detroit-billed Chaos A.D. member, one of the federation's three founders, a former Television champion and co-owner, who came back after almost three and a half years to referee the World title match at Genocide and teamed with Dazz again at Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: The federation's own About page names him a founder; Genocide (22 October 2006) announces his return after almost three and a half years away, and Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007) reunites him with Dazz.

name: Jake Fury
caption: The Hardcore Icon, in the federation from its first month in January 2003, a Hall of Fame inductee and Chaos champion who retired on the last Ultimate Chaos by winning a Barbwire Massacre match.

tenures.source: Its own Hall of Fame page puts him in the federation from the start in January 2003; Genocide has him tagging with Fuel, and Ultimate Chaos stages his retirement match against Hall Jarrett.

name: Fuel
caption: A Hull, England wrestler and two-time International champion who lost the title to Christian Connolly in a sixty-minute Iron Man match at Genocide, where he also teamed with Jake Fury as the Icons of Extreme.

tenures.source: Appears as International champion on Genocide, 22 October 2006, where he loses the title.

identity.note: Name collision only: no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's own record ties this character to the same-named records already held at other wings.

name: John Thomas
caption: A Generation Xtreme wrestler from Gainesville, Florida, billed first as the Freak and then as the Hardcore Assassin, who won the 2007 Death Wish battle royal and challenged Priest for the World title at Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Teams with X-Factor as Generation Xtreme on Genocide (22 October 2006); on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007) he is billed as the Death Wish 2007 winner and challenges for the World Heavyweight title.

identity.note: Name collision only: no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's own record ties this character to the same-named records already held at other wings.

Moniker collision only: The Freak and the Hardcore Assassin are generic billings used across many federations; this John Thomas is billed by his own name, from Gainesville, Florida, as a member of Generation Xtreme, and no record here names any of those wrestlers.

name: X-Factor
caption: A 178-pound Generation Xtreme wrestler from Ankeny, Iowa, billed as the winner of Eliminator Elite 2005 and a former World champion, who lost the International title to The Punk on the last Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Challenges Priest for the World title on Genocide (22 October 2006) and defends the International title against The Punk on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

identity.note: Name collision only: no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's own record ties this character to the same-named records already held at other wings.

name: The Punk
caption: A cocky Hit Squad wrestler billed from Manhattan who held the Tag Team title with Roman Steeler and won the International championship from X-Factor on the last Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Defends the Tag Team title with Roman Steeler on Genocide (22 October 2006) and wins the International title on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

name: Roman Steeler
caption: A 280-pound Hit Squad wrestler billed from Liverpool, England, who rides a motorcycle to the ring, held the Tag Team title with The Punk, and beat Marty Pillman on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Tag Team champion with The Punk on Genocide (22 October 2006); wrestles Marty Pillman on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).
Chapters 2 and 3 of the Vitriol and Ambrosia serial and Dazz's Nightmare Before Christmas roleplay put him in MCW with Vash the Stampede as The Hit Squad, facing Vitriol and Ambrosia.

identity.note: The same Roman Steeler: the serial pairs him with Vash the Stampede as The Hit Squad, the pair the predecessor's own Genocide broadcast bills as Hit Squad members, and calls them veterans of many matches against Priest.

name: Vash the Stampede
caption: A Hit Squad member who enters to the Trigun theme firing a gun loaded with blanks, beaten by Hirvon at Genocide and sent in as the Hit Squad's smallest wrestler against the champions at Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Loses to Hirvon on Genocide (22 October 2006); on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007) the commentary calls him the Hit Squad's smallest wrestler, with one of the group's managers as his partner.
Chapter 2 of the Vitriol and Ambrosia serial puts him in the tag battle royale as one of The Hit Squad with Roman Steeler.

identity.note: The same Vash the Stampede: the serial pairs him with Roman Steeler as The Hit Squad, the pair the predecessor's own Genocide broadcast bills.

name: Hirvon
caption: A 435-pound big man billed from the Unknown, who beat Vash the Stampede at Genocide with a moonsault and is mentor to the masked Carnage.

tenures.source: Beats Vash the Stampede on Genocide (22 October 2006) and brings Carnage to the ring for the Cruiserweight title match.

name: Carnage
caption: A masked 225-pound cruiserweight billed from parts unknown and brought to the ring by Hirvon, who ran from the opening bell and was the first man eliminated from the Cruiserweight title match at Genocide.

tenures.source: Wrestles the Cruiserweight title elimination match on Genocide (22 October 2006).

identity.note: Name collision only: no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's own record ties this character to the same-named records already held at other wings.
Name collision only: a generic name; this masked Carnage, Hirvon's charge billed from parts unknown, carries nothing that ties him to those records.

name: Michael Machete
caption: The Long Island-billed Cruiserweight champion on both surviving broadcasts, a former Hit Squad member who kept the title against Ken Sandwave and Carnage at Genocide and against Neptune at Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Defends the Cruiserweight title on Genocide (22 October 2006) and on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

name: Ken Sandwave
caption: A Venice Beach, California challenger billed as the All New Ace, who eliminated Carnage but lost the Cruiserweight title match to Michael Machete at Genocide.

tenures.source: Challenges for the Cruiserweight title on Genocide (22 October 2006).

name: Faith
caption: A Las Vegas-billed Women's champion, Hall of Fame inductee and the first woman to hold the World Heavyweight title, fiancee of Dazz, who lost the Women's title to Syd Ashley in a gauntlet at Genocide.

tenures.source: Its own Hall of Fame page makes her the first Women's champion and the first woman World Heavyweight champion; Genocide (22 October 2006) takes the Women's title from her and Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007) shows her champion again.

Its champions page (captured 7 January 2008): a challenger for the Tag Team titles on 03/11/2007; its Mayhem card of 3 December 2007 bills her in a dark match; Dazz's roleplays of 2009 and 2010 follow her return, her marriage to him and its end.

identity.note: Name collision only: no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's own record ties this character to the same-named records already held at other wings.

The same Faith: Dazz's roleplays call her the first CWF Women's champion and the first woman to hold its World title, his fiancee then wife, and bring her to MCW among the CWF-contracted talent; the predecessor wing's own pages bill her the same way.

name: Lexi
caption: A Suffolk, Virginia Diva, first into the Women's gauntlet at Genocide and the winner over Syd Ashley on Ultimate Chaos, where the broadcast calls her recent behaviour towards Syd psychotic.

tenures.source: First entrant against Faith in the Women's gauntlet on Genocide (22 October 2006); beats Syd Ashley on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

name: Kira
caption: A Los Angeles Diva billed as Faith's sister and a former Women's champion, second into the Genocide gauntlet.

tenures.source: Wrestles Faith in the Women's gauntlet on Genocide (22 October 2006); the broadcast says it took her a year to take the title from her sister, who won it back a few months later.

name: Skye Estado
caption: A Los Angeles Diva billed from Hollywood's party scene, who went into the Women's title match on both surviving broadcasts as the challenger and lost both.

tenures.source: Third into the gauntlet on Genocide (22 October 2006); challenges Faith on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

Dazz's Livewire six-person roleplay (4 February 2010) puts her in a Livewire trio with Brittany Lohan and Aaron Dietrich, has her lose a ladder match for the Dedication briefcase, a tag match with Vitriol and a return match to Nick Cagero, and recalls her CWF Women's title challenges against Faith, Kira, Syd Ashley and Lexi.

identity.note: The same Skye Estado: the roleplay says she worked in CWF and failed to take the Women's title from Faith, Kira, Syd Ashley and Lexi, which matches the predecessor wing's own Diva challenger.

name: Syd Ashley
caption: A Toronto Diva who won the Women's title from Faith at Genocide after being clotheslined by Phil King on the way to the ring, and lost to Lexi on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Wins the Women's championship on Genocide (22 October 2006); wrestles Lexi on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007), billed as the former Women's champion.

name: Phil King
caption: A huge bodyguard at Faith's side in the Genocide gauntlet, who clotheslined Syd Ashley before her entrance and was booked in a three-way on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Accompanies Faith on Genocide (22 October 2006); named on the Ultimate Chaos card (3 April 2007).

name: Christian Connolly
caption: The Suntan Superman of Talent Inc, a Hall of Fame inductee and three-time World champion whose own Hall of Fame page bills him as Christian Cage, who won the International title from Fuel in an Iron Man match at Genocide.

tenures.source: Its own Hall of Fame page, titled Christian Cage, names him the first World champion of the federation's second run; Genocide (22 October 2006) and Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007) bill him as Christian Connolly.

identity.note: Name collision only: no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's own record ties this character to the same-named records already held at other wings.

Those rows are other federations' portrayals of the real wrestler billed Christian Cage. This is an original character of a federation whose rules barred real wrestlers: Christian Connolly, the Suntan Superman, billed from Edmonton and Norfolk, Virginia, whose earlier ring name Christian Cage the broadcast calls his own former name. A shared ring name with a portrayal is never identity.
Moniker collision only: The Paragon is one of this character's many billings; those Paragons share nothing else on record with him.

name: Priest
caption: A 328-pound World Heavyweight champion from Houston, Texas, who beat Christian Connolly for the title, kept it against X-Factor at Genocide and against John Thomas on the last Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Its own About page names him a contender for the World title in 2005; he defends it on Genocide (22 October 2006) and Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

Its champions page (captured 7 January 2008) names Priest the Brutality champion since All Hallows Annihilation (19/11/07); Dazz's Legends Match and Motor City contender roleplays call him the last CWF World champion before the sale and merge that formed MCW.

identity.note: Name collision only: no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's own record ties this character to the same-named records already held at other wings.

The same Priest: Dazz's Legends Match and Motor City contender roleplays call him the predecessor's last World Heavyweight champion, which its own last broadcast shows him keeping, and say he came to MCW when the buyer took on his contract; MCW's champions page has him its Brutality champion in November 2007.

name: Dark Rayne
caption: A Hall of Fame inductee who entered in February 2005 as Cloudburst, won the International title, took on the Dark Rayne persona after a feud with Turmoil, and teamed with Christian Connolly as Talent Inc.

tenures.source: Its own Hall of Fame page dates his entry to February 2005; Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007) has him back with Talent Inc against Chaos A.D.

name: Iceman
caption: A Las Vegas magician-act wrestler, the big half of the New Two Man Power Trip, who challenged for the Tag Team titles on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Challenges for the Tag Team title on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

identity.note: Name collision only: no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's own record ties this character to the same-named records already held at other wings.
Name collision only: a generic name; this Iceman is the Las Vegas magician half of the New Two Man Power Trip, and nothing on record ties him to those wrestlers.

name: Simon Steeler
caption: A jewelled-cape magician billed as Sensational Simon Steeler and S3, the other half of the New Two Man Power Trip, who took the loss in the Tag Team title match on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Challenges for the Tag Team title on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007) and takes the loss.

name: Jay D Scott
caption: A Hit Squad manager who danced to the ring from the team's Hit Street bus and, not being a trained wrestler, was told to stay in the corner for the whole Tag Team title match on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Represents the Hit Squad in the Tag Team title match on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007), where the commentary calls him one of the group's managers and not a trained wrestler.

name: Neptune
caption: The newest member of the Hit Squad, billed from Sin City, who lost the Cruiserweight title challenge to Michael Machete on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Challenges Michael Machete for the Cruiserweight title on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

identity.note: Name collision only: no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's own record ties this character to the same-named records already held at other wings.

name: Marty Pillman
caption: A 200-pound wrestler billed from Orlando, Florida, who lost to Roman Steeler on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Wrestles Roman Steeler on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

name: Hall Jarrett
caption: A young 238-pound wrestler with a pyrotechnic entrance, Jake Fury's opponent in the Barbwire Massacre match that closed Fury's career on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Loses to Jake Fury in the Barbwire Massacre match on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

name: Tommy Chaos
caption: A retired Chaos A.D. founding member who ran the federation as President from September 2004 and was the first man eliminated from the staff triple threat on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Its own About page names him President from September 2004; Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007) puts him in the staff triple threat.

name: Jaymz Marshall
caption: A retired wrestler and former NLCW Commissioner brought in as Aggression General Manager in January 2005, billed the self-proclaimed Whole F'n Show, who won the staff triple threat on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Its own About page names him General Manager of Aggression from January 2005; he wins the staff encounter on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

name: Lord Phillippe DeMontfort
caption: The businessman who bought the federation's name in 2004, reopened it that September, and sold his majority shares in March 2007, billed on the last Ultimate Chaos as its Chairman and owner from July 2004.

tenures.source: Its own About page has him buy the name and reopen it with the first Aggression on 12 September 2004; Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007) says he sold his shares the month before.

name: Logan Kincaide
caption: A former Assistant General Manager of Aggression, last seen about a year before, brought back as special guest referee for the staff triple threat on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Referees the staff encounter on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

name: Anthony Wallace
caption: The buyer of the Chairman's majority shares, shown in a skybox interview on Ultimate Chaos saying he will rename the company Motor City Wrestling and move it to Detroit.

tenures.source: Interviewed in the skybox on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

Dazz's roleplays name Anthony Wallace as the man who bought the majority shares in March 2007 and took on the predecessor's contracts, MCW's owner until he could no longer give it his full attention; Jacob Laymon signs the fed's news as its owner by 22 November 2007.

identity.note: The same Anthony Wallace: the predecessor's own last broadcast shows its buyer, billed with that name, announce the new name, Motor City Wrestling; Dazz's roleplays make him MCW's first owner.

name: Phil Sullivan
caption: The play-by-play voice of both surviving broadcasts, who calls Genocide and the last Ultimate Chaos beside Derrick Grimes.

tenures.source: Opens both Genocide (22 October 2006) and Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007) on commentary.

name: Derrick Grimes
caption: The partisan colour commentator of both surviving broadcasts, billed The Man, who admits on the last show that a former owner once fired him.

tenures.source: Co-hosts Genocide (22 October 2006) and Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

name: Lucinda Welch
caption: The ring announcer on both surviving broadcasts, who introduces every contest on Genocide and Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Announces every contest on Genocide (22 October 2006) and Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

name: Chris Reid
caption: A federation interviewer who talks to the new owner in the skybox on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Interviews Anthony Wallace on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

name: Kimberlea Close
caption: A federation interviewer who talks to Jake Fury before his retirement match on Ultimate Chaos.

tenures.source: Interviews Jake Fury on Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007).

name: Nemesis
caption: A big man in the federation from its first month, the first CWF double champion with the Tag Team and Television titles at once, and the host of a talk show called nTV.

tenures.source: Its own Hall of Fame page puts him in the federation from the start, in January 2003, and lists his title wins.

identity.note: Name collision only: no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's own record ties this character to the same-named records already held at other wings.

Same host and a shared name, nothing more: the Classic Wrestling Federation's Nemesis, billed Da Big Man, held that federation's World title in 1998 and 1999; this Nemesis's own Hall of Fame page starts him in this federation in January 2003 and lists titles here, in the CWA and in NLCW, never the Classic federation's. A big man in both tellings is description, not a shared moniker. Revisit if a document names both.

name: Dana Morris
caption: The second name on the Women's title history, who took the belt from Faith at CWF Impact on 1 May 2005.

tenures.source: Named as the winner of the Women's title on its own title-history page, 1 May 2005, CWF Impact.

name: Dragon Master
caption: Kodo-san, a friend of Dark Rayne who was recruited into Talent Inc as the Dragon Master.

tenures.source: Its own About page and Dark Rayne's Hall of Fame page name him a member of Talent Inc, undated, in 2005.

name: Johnny Speede
caption: A protege of Dark Rayne, recruited into Talent Inc.

tenures.source: Its own About page and Dark Rayne's Hall of Fame page name him a member of Talent Inc, undated, in 2005.
